question: Name the Indian social reformer who played a crucial role in the passing of the Age of Consent Bill, 1891.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Behramji Malabari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Behramji Malabari was an Indian poet, publicist, and social reformer born on 18th May 1853.
 
• He played a pivotal role in advocating for the rights of women, especially in his campaign against child marriage and for the passage of the Age of Consent Act, 1891.
 
• Malabari's efforts brought attention to the plight of young girls who were subjected to early marriage and its detrimental effects on their health and well-being.
 
• His activism and writings were instrumental in influencing the British authorities to raise the age of consent for girls from 10 to 12 years through the Age of Consent Act, 1891.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Age of Consent Act, 1891**

 
 
• The Age of Consent Act, 1891 was a legislation enacted during the British colonial rule in India.
 
• The Act raised the age of consent for sexual intercourse for girls from 10 to 12 years.
 
• This was one of the early legal reforms aimed at protecting young girls from exploitation and child marriage.
 
• The Act was a significant milestone in the history of social reforms in India, highlighting the growing awareness and efforts towards improving women's rights and conditions.
 
 
 
• **Behramji Malabari's Contributions**
 
 
• Besides his work on the Age of Consent Act, Malabari was also known for his efforts in social reforms such as widow remarriage and the fight against the practice of purdah (veil).
 
• He founded the "Seva Sadan" in 1908, an institution dedicated to the welfare of women and children.
 
• Malabari's literary works, including his poetry and publicist writings, played a crucial role in spreading social awareness and advocating for reforms.
 
• His book, "Notes on Infant Marriage and Enforced Widowhood," published in 1887, was influential in bringing the issues of child marriage and enforced widowhood to the forefront of social discourse.
